prompt: In plain terms, explain why a distributed database might show a stale value right after a write, and why that's called 'eventual consistency.'
reference_facts: In an eventually consistent system, a write to one node takes time to propagate to all other nodes.
During that propagation window, a read from a different node can return the old, stale value.
The system is called 'eventually consistent' because all nodes converge to the same value once propagation finishes.
